questions.question: In the study by Schnall and colleagues on disgust and moral judgments, what were the two independent variables?

answers.text: Disgust (clean vs. messy room) and private body consciousness (high vs. low)
Disgust (clean vs. messy room) and moral judgment severity
Private body consciousness and hand washing behavior
Room cleanliness and participant emotional state

questions.question: What is a factorial design?

answers.text: An experiment where each level of one independent variable is combined with each level of the others to produce all possible combinations
An experiment that includes only one independent variable with multiple levels
A study that focuses on the relationship between two correlated variables
A research design that uses only non-manipulated independent variables

questions.question: How many conditions would a 3 × 2 factorial design have?

answers.text: 6 conditions
5 conditions
9 conditions
3 conditions

questions.question: In a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design, how many independent variables are there?

answers.text: 3 independent variables
2 independent variables
6 independent variables
8 independent variables

questions.question: What is a between-subjects factorial design?

answers.text: A design where all independent variables are manipulated between subjects, with each participant tested in only one condition
A design where all independent variables are manipulated within subjects, with each participant tested in all conditions
A design where one independent variable is manipulated between subjects and another within subjects
A design where participants are randomly assigned to different experimenters

questions.question: What is a mixed factorial design?

answers.text: A design where one independent variable is manipulated between subjects and another is manipulated within subjects
A design that combines experimental and correlational methods
A design where all variables are non-manipulated
A design that uses both quantitative and qualitative data

questions.question: In the Brown and colleagues study on hypochondriasis and word recall, what type of independent variable was hypochondriasis?

answers.text: A non-manipulated independent variable (participant variable)
A manipulated between-subjects variable
A manipulated within-subjects variable
A dependent variable

questions.question: Why can causal conclusions only be drawn about manipulated independent variables and not non-manipulated ones?

answers.text: Because non-manipulated variables may be correlated with third variables that could actually cause the observed effect
Because non-manipulated variables are always measured after the dependent variable
Because non-manipulated variables have lower statistical power
Because non-manipulated variables cannot be included in factorial designs

questions.question: What is a main effect in a factorial design?

answers.text: The effect of one independent variable on the dependent variable, averaged across all levels of the other independent variable(s)
The combined effect of all independent variables on the dependent variable
The effect that occurs only when two independent variables interact
The most statistically significant effect in the experiment

questions.question: What is an interaction effect?

answers.text: When the effect of one independent variable depends on the level of another independent variable
When two independent variables have additive effects on the dependent variable
When participants interact with the researcher during the experiment
When the dependent variable influences the independent variable

questions.question: In Schnall and colleagues' study, the effect of disgust on moral judgments depended on private body consciousness. What does this describe?

answers.text: An interaction between disgust and private body consciousness
A main effect of disgust only
A main effect of private body consciousness only
A confounding variable

questions.question: What is a spreading interaction?

answers.text: An interaction where one independent variable has an effect at one level of another independent variable but not at the other level, or has a stronger effect at one level than the other
An interaction where the effects of one variable are in opposite directions at different levels of another variable
An interaction where effects gradually increase across all conditions
An interaction that affects multiple dependent variables simultaneously

questions.question: What is a crossover interaction?

answers.text: An interaction where one independent variable has opposite effects at different levels of another independent variable
An interaction where two variables have the same effect across all conditions
An interaction that occurs midway through an experiment
An interaction between a within-subjects and between-subjects variable

questions.question: In Gilliland's study on caffeine and test performance, introverts performed better without caffeine while extraverts performed better with caffeine. What type of interaction is this?

answers.text: A crossover interaction
A spreading interaction
A main effect only
A simple effect

questions.question: What is a simple effects analysis?

answers.text: An analysis that examines the effect of each independent variable at each level of the other independent variable(s)
An analysis that only examines main effects
An analysis used when no interaction is present
An analysis that averages effects across all conditions

questions.question: When is it necessary to conduct a simple effects analysis?

answers.text: When an interaction is present
Only when main effects are absent
In all factorial designs regardless of results
Only in within-subjects designs

questions.question: How many simple effects analyses would need to be examined in a 2 × 2 factorial design?

answers.text: 4 simple effects
2 simple effects
8 simple effects
6 simple effects

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of including multiple independent variables in a single experiment?

answers.text: It allows researchers to answer questions about whether the effect of one independent variable depends on the level of another
It reduces the need for statistical analysis
It eliminates the need for random assignment
It guarantees that causal conclusions can be drawn about all variables

questions.question: If a factorial design includes only non-manipulated independent variables, what type of study is it?

answers.text: A non-experimental study
A true experiment
A quasi-experiment only if it has two variables
A within-subjects experiment

questions.question: In a 4 × 5 factorial design, how many distinct conditions would there be?

answers.text: 20 conditions
9 conditions
45 conditions
10 conditions
